design_conclusions.conclusion: Raw-resource intake, processing, visible output buffers, distinct feeder lanes and a dedicated sales outfeed are supported by primary A.
Automatic supply and manual/helper carry coexist; connecting new belts must preserve customer queues and worker approaches.
Raw-looking logs, meat and whole fish are sold in some sources; product acceptance must be counter-specific.
Cash collection is spatially separate from goods movement.
Universal upgradable storage house with classified receiving docks, inventory ledger, reserved dispatch and overflow rules is a Havenline extension.
Smart sorters, filtered splitters, mergers, bridge/liftgate safety, throughput tiers and full-buffer backpressure require explicit design and implementation checks.
Production should deliver directly to a needing downstream station where possible; reserve/surplus can route to store without mandatory warehouse round trips.

unresolved: 13 full YouTube streams unavailable; storyboard-only coverage cannot certify motion.
No source proves every requested storage-house interface.
No authoritative numeric belt heights/widths, rates, stack limits or machine recipes obtained from footage.
No source proves conservation, blocked output, invalid input, loop prevention or stall recovery; those are acceptance requirements for implementation, not research findings.
